sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro Model Card (June 27, 2025)
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact June 27 Pro card distinguishes GA, Experimental 03-25 and Preview 05-06. Architecture is sparse MoE Transformer, with qualitative per-token routing and improvements over the earlier Gemini architecture; neither a total nor active numerical size is given. Its exact-model tables contain performance and safety results, not parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro — Gemini API
sources.evidence: Exact stable ID gemini-2.5-pro: 1,048,576 input tokens, 65,536 output tokens; audio, image, video, text and PDF inputs; text output; thinking and function calling supported. September 22, 2026 documentation retains access for previous users; no endpoint was tested. Reopened October 27, 2026: the exact stable-model specification table still has no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes
sources.evidence: Dates the 03-25 experimental release to March 25, the 06-05 preview to June 5, and stable gemini-2.5-pro to June 17, 2025. It separately records subsequent redirects of older preview IDs.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5: Updates to our family of thinking models
sources.evidence: June 17, 2025 GA announcement explicitly states there are no changes from the 06-05 Pro preview, providing an exact underlying-model identity bridge. Reopened October 27, 2026. This is valid same-model lineage, but the June preview has no published count to inherit.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Proprietary service terms govern access and prohibit extraction of underlying model components, including parameter weights; the page does not offer an open-weight model license.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 technical report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 full-text inspection: section 2.1 specifies sparse MoE routing but no numerical total, active size or expert dimensions. Table 2 explicitly maps Gemini 2.5 Pro to gemini-2.5-pro; Tables 1 and 3–6 compare capabilities rather than parameters. The 22-billion vision model and trillion-parameter Switch Transformer occurrences are cited external research. Flash-size distillation does not establish a known-size Pro base.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Card (October 2026)
sources.evidence: Latest-generation first-party architecture and evaluation sections checked for retrospective disclosures; no Gemini 2.5 Pro parameter counts are supplied. Rechecked October 27, 2026 against the complete freshly retrieved card; no retrospective total or activated count found.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 2.5 Pro record
sources.evidence: Baseline source followed and raw record retrieved. Its June 17 date describes the stable endpoint launch; technical fields were independently checked against Google sources.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 review of the full later report. Section 6.1.3, printed page 211, compares Gemini 2.5 Pro with the smaller 2.5 Flash in prompt-injection robustness. It supplies only a qualitative size relationship, with no total or active count; other parameter mentions concern security or knowledge.

sources.title: Google Transparency Report, Foundation Model Transparency Index December 2025
sources.publisher: Stanford CRFM, including Google developer responses
sources.evidence: Freshly located and opened October 27. In indicators 35–37 Google describes Gemini 2.5 Pro architecture refinements and continuation of Gemini 2.0; no numerical size or specific unchanged base is supplied. The evaluator explicitly records size absent. Indicators 21 and 38 publish Google's rationale for withholding compute-related detail alongside parameters. This corroborates the original documentation and does not replace the later-disclosure search.

sources.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models for 2D Object Detection under SOTIF Conditions
sources.publisher: Zhou et al., independent evaluation research
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model search surfaced a 128B claim in Table I. Opened the paper and checked section II-C and references: no developer source supports the Gemini 2.5 Pro size. It is an unsupported secondary assertion, not accepted nominal evidence.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Fresh count-estimation lead opened October 27. Section 6.3 Table 2 estimates Gemini 2.5 Pro effective knowledge capacity at about 3.0T open-model-equivalent parameters with a 943B–9.6T interval. These are black-box factual-capacity calibration estimates, not Google specifications or measured parameter counts. Appendix E leaves its known-size field blank. No estimate is substituted for the catalog count.

developer.note: Google publishes the model; development is attributed to Google DeepMind and the Gemini Team.

family.note: Retain the catalog’s normalized Pro subfamily key within the official Gemini 2.5 family.

release_date.note: Earliest public release of the underlying GA model: June 5 preview. Stable ID launched June 17 with explicitly no model changes. March 25 was an earlier distinct experimental revision; later redirects do not establish earlier checkpoint identity.

open_weights.note: Hosted proprietary model distribution; no public checkpoint or open-weight license in the reviewed official release/model documentation.

license.note: Descriptive model/service classification. Documentation and sample-code licenses do not apply to model weights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model total-size and named-base searches, original card/report and later primary comparisons found no supported nominal total. Google explicitly equates the June 5 preview with GA, but neither has a numerical count. Earlier-generation architectural continuity is not a known-size unchanged base. Investigated an uncited 128B table and black-box effective-capacity estimates; neither establishes a developer specification. Null reflects absent numerical evidence, not a requirement for exact tensor accounting.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-parameter searches and later exact-model comparison checks found no numerical active count. Sparse expert routing is explicit, but neither an active count nor dimensions and routing quantities sufficient to establish one are supplied. Later Google tables report capabilities and safety, with only qualitative size comparisons; active parameters are not inferred from total size or third-party capacity estimates.

architecture.note: Explicit sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer. The report’s Table 2 connects the described Pro model to this exact stable API ID.

context_window.note: Documented input-token limit; 65,536 output tokens is a separate limit, not an addition to this catalog value.

modalities.note: Use the exact stable endpoint specification. The report’s qualified audio-generation variants do not establish audio output for this ID.

reasoning.note: Thinking supported; adaptive thinking is explicitly documented for the 06-05 and stable model.

tool_call.note: Exact endpoint lists function calling; the report independently identifies tool use.

patch.notes: The GA model first appeared as the June 5, 2025 preview; Google explicitly states the June 17 stable release uses the same model. March 25 and May 6 were earlier revisions. Sparse MoE Transformer; total and active parameter counts are undisclosed in the reviewed sources. Context is the documented 1,048,576-token input limit; output limit is separate.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit completed October 27, 2026. Total and active counts remain explicitly null after original source reinspection, exact-model and lineage searches, later Google comparison checks, and investigation of unsupported 128B and black-box capacity-estimation leads. Google's contemporaneous FMTI responses corroborate nondisclosure. All unrelated field assessments are preserved.
